import/extract vs live-query vs Power BI Direct Lake (reading Delta tables in OneLake directly) and the load each puts on the warehouse
headless BI serving one metrics layer to many tools

items.item: LookML is the Looker Modeling Language, used to create semantic data models that describe dimensions, aggregates, calculations and data relationships
LookML is a dependency language, independent of particular SQL dialects
Direct Lake loads data from OneLake's Delta tables directly into memory for high-performance interactive analysis, for large data volumes
a Direct Lake refresh copies only metadata ("framing"), unlike an Import refresh which copies the whole data volume
Direct Lake on SQL analytics endpoints falls back to DirectQuery mode when it can't load data directly from a Delta table
column loading is named "transcoding" in Microsoft's own documentation, subject to documented Fabric capacity guardrails by SKU
an open-source modern data exploration and visualization platform connecting to any SQL-based database, including cloud-native databases at petabyte scale

items.item: an open-source business intelligence tool connecting to many popular databases, letting users ask questions and see answers as charts or tables

sources.source: Tableau Help — Tutorial: Get Started with Tableau Desktop (tableau.com unreachable, documentation subdomain substituted)

items.item: Tableau Desktop builds views, maps, dashboards and stories from data, shared via Tableau Server, Tableau Cloud or Tableau Public

The hook's 'cost triples overnight with no change to the dashboard' is the load-bearing detail: it isolates the query mode as the only variable that changed, which is exactly what the predict step and the reveal are teaching the learner to notice first in a real incident.

Naming Looker/LookML as the 'commercial ancestor' of Chapter 3's generic semantic-layer idea matters because it tells the learner the concept predates this course's own vocabulary for it, not the reverse — LookML did not borrow the idea from a semantic layer, the semantic-layer idea is this course's generic name for what LookML and tools like it already did.

Import/extract and live-query are opposite trade-offs on the same axis (freshness versus warehouse load), not two unrelated features — a learner who can place Direct Lake's transcoding as a third point on that same axis (near-import speed, near-live freshness, at the cost of Fabric-specific constraints) has understood the mechanism, not just memorized three names.

Headless BI is not a feature any of the five named tools implements — it is what becomes possible once topic 8's compiled metric exists, independent of which tool reads it; this topic's own phrase for the idea deliberately does not appear in any of the five vendors' own documentation.

This refresher's own 'Leaves out' line (no tool's modeling-language syntax, no acceleration engines, no renegotiation of the metric-ownership process) is evidence the refresher is doing its one job — naming the tool-side half of topic 8's contract — rather than drifting into a feature tour or re-teaching topic 8 or topic 10's material.

The Prove It step's cross-tool metric drift scenario generalizes beyond Looker/Metabase specifically: any two tools reading from the same warehouse but not the same compiled metric can drift apart in exactly this way, regardless of which two tools they are.

Because tableau.com's marketing site is unreachable in this sandbox, this topic's Tableau categorization traces to Tableau's own documentation subdomain (help.tableau.com) rather than its marketing copy — this topic's FACT-CHECK states that substitution plainly rather than implying the marketing page was read.

The commercial/open-source split named in this topic (Looker, Power BI, Tableau commercial; Superset, Metabase open-source) is a licensing distinction, not a capability ranking — nothing in any of the five vendors' own quoted documentation claims one category is more capable than the other, only that they're operated differently.

A reader who only remembers 'live mode is slower' from this topic has missed the actual lesson: live-query is not slower in general, it simply moves the cost from a scheduled refresh to every single interaction, which is a cost-timing trade-off, not a universal speed penalty.

Direct Lake's own documented fallback to DirectQuery (claim 5) is itself evidence that 'zero import, always fast' is not an unconditional promise even within Microsoft's own stack — the overview page names specific conditions (a SQL view, SQL-based granular access control) under which the fast path isn't available, which is the same kind of documented limit this chapter's other topics take seriously rather than treating a vendor's headline feature as absolute.

This topic's own outcomes line ('classify a given BI setup... and predict which puts load on the warehouse and when') is testable against the hook itself: a learner who has internalized the three modes can explain the tripled cost without this topic ever stating the mechanism a second time after the reveal steps.
